Ticket T-0073: Tests for quarantine moves, retry context, and partial-wave integration
R-017 One bad ticket can't hold a wave.
  - Failed ticket outputs move to a quarantine folder automatically, and the retry gets them as read-only context.
  - Passing tickets in a wave integrate through the merge queue while the failing one is bisected out.
Acceptance (each line has a tag; the ticket is done only when every line is met):
- AC1: Failed ticket outputs move to a quarantine folder automatically, and the retry gets them as read-only context.
- AC2: Passing tickets in a wave integrate through the merge queue while the failing one is bisected out.
Put the tag in the title of the test that checks a line, for example test('AC2: rejects a reply link with a bad host'). A line no test can check (a size limit, a visual rule) may have no test: a reviewer will check it against your code.
Use the dependency versions in package.json; do not assume other major versions.
Watch out for (background from past lessons; it does not change the task, the files or the outputs):
- A worker asked to add or change tested code needs a way to run the checks itself, inside a sandbox, and must report which checks it ran. [manifest, sandbox, test, worker-output]
- Integration is all-or-nothing; every precondition, including a mutants file's shape, is checked before the first file is written. [manifest, mutation-testing, retries, test, worker-output]
- Mutants only count against a base that is actually green. [integration, manifest, mutation-testing]
Work only on the files you own; report the ticket id.
acceptance: Failed ticket outputs move to a quarantine folder automatically, and the retry gets them as read-only context.
